title: Declared local LLM hosts
description: The local inference servers this fleet will talk to, declared once for memory-layer, commitwork/admin and overwatch-layer. Every host speaks the OpenAI HTTP API, which is what makes this a declaration rather than a set of adapters — a new host is a row, not a struct. The required fields are the ones that stop a consumer from asserting something it did not measure: `licence` and `openSource` so an open-tooling claim about this fleet can be checked rather than repeated, `capabilities` so nothing assumes /v1/embeddings exists on a chat-only server, and `portIsShared` because llama.cpp, llamafile, LocalAI and mlx-lm all default to 8080 and a consumer that probes 8080 and reports a host name is naming something the probe cannot distinguish. Written without $ref/definitions on purpose: monitor/registry.mjs implements neither and refuses a schema that uses them, so sharing subschemas would silently disable this gate rather than tidy it.

detection.description: Why a successful probe does not identify a host. Prose, but load-bearing prose: it is the reason `portIsShared` exists.

default.description: The host named in documentation and used when nothing is detected and nothing is configured. Distinct from the head of probeOrder on purpose — see defaultRationale.

probeOrder.description: Detection order. Ordered by how unambiguous a hit is, NOT by preference, so that the first answer is the most trustworthy one rather than the most wanted one.

enabledByDefault.description: Whether a declared runner is live without the operator turning it on. False, and the reason is in enabledByDefaultRationale and the per-host exposureNote fields. Declared rather than hardcoded so the security posture is a readable fact and flipping it is a visible edit.

contextNote.description: Records a protection that removing ollama cost: per-request num_ctx/keep_alive have no OpenAI equivalent, so KV-cache sizing is now the operator's server launch flag and nothing here enforces it. Kept as a field rather than a comment so it survives an edit that tidies prose.

removed.description: Hosts deliberately dropped. Kept so 'why is X not supported' has a dated answer instead of a silence that reads like an oversight.

baseUrl.description: The project's documented default. Every consumer must allow an override; a wrong value here costs a config line and is not a correctness property.

api.description: Deliberately single-valued. A host needing another request shape does not belong in this file — that was ollama, and carrying it meant every consumer branched on engine type forever. Widening this enum is the decision to reintroduce that branch, so it should be hard rather than incidental.

licence.description: As stated upstream. Recorded so an open-source claim about this fleet is checkable. 'proprietary' is a permitted and honest value.

openSource.description: Its own field rather than derived from `licence`, so a reader filtering for open tooling does not have to parse licence strings and guess.

portIsShared.description: True when another host in this file defaults to the same port. A consumer probing a shared port MUST report the host as unidentified: the protocol is identical, so nothing about the response distinguishes them.

capabilities.description: Declared narrow on purpose. mlx-lm serves chat and not embeddings; a consumer that assumes /v1/embeddings there gets a 404. A declared capability is still a claim about the server's DEFAULT configuration and must be probed before use — llama-server only serves embeddings when started with --embedding.

bindsAllInterfacesByDefault.description: REQUIRED, because it is the fact that decides whether starting this server is a local act or a network one. localai, vllm and sglang bind 0.0.0.0 out of the box, so launching one publishes an unauthenticated generation endpoint to the LAN. A host added without answering this would be enabled on the same footing as a loopback-only one.

fetchesModelsOnDemand.description: REQUIRED. True when a request naming an unknown model id can cause a download. It turns a generation request into an egress event, which is a different thing to authorise.
